correctness.rationale: Subtract the published Knott and natural digit-gap recurrences. The difference state (d_i,d_i-d_(i-1)) has the two explicitly nonnegative transition matrices. All parity/cost transition inequalities against the Fibonacci envelope are checked at the base costs and proved for all larger costs by monotone Fibonacci increments. The endpoint exponents of every even Lucas interval give span 4j, and the no-consecutive-ones witness 2F_(2j+1) attains the bound. The minimum 1 follows from strict state growth. An exact-coordinate checker reproduces all eight first intervals, 2,213 integers, and 9,506 finite inequality cases. Finite checks are not used to infer the infinite claim.

value.rationale: The sharp worst-case excess of two natural finite base-phi counting conventions is a motivated interval extremum. This complete all-j result strengthens isolated Fibonacci/Lucas values, explains a genuine Fibonacci growth law through universal state bounds and provides explicit sharp witnesses. It does not merely reindex the existing recurrence.
